chapter: Gillespie and Carter on John Collins
title: Gillespie on Collins's practicing and harp-like voicings
summary: Gillespie says no book shows what Collins does, praises his constant practice, sophisticated progressions and a recent private harp-like demonstration.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x:
You see, what John knows and what he does there are no books, there are no books that will show you what he does because that guy has been practicing for the last -- oh man, he's been practicing every since I've been knowing him and see I've been knowing him since the early '40s, and he puts in time on that instrument.
See, he makes things on that guitar that nobody --

progressions and voice. You know, a lot of guys make the same progression, you know, progression like going from E minor to A 7 flat or with an added 11 and this that John, nobody is as sophisticated as he is and nobody has been that sophisticated.

You see, this guy -- that guitar now is like -- well like he's got three hands now. He's got one picking the guitar, he's got one fingering and the guitar is another hand. He's three handed, this motherfucker.

The other day he came by -- came by where I spent the night, the other night when he was behind us and he came by over there and so we had a little aside and I was telling him about my religious faith and everything --

-- and see this guy plays with Jimmy Smith -- was playing, he was playing for hours back in the back room there. John took that guitar and came up in the living room and this is where he and I were sitting there. Boy, this is -- the way that he plays, his voicing on there is like a harp.

It's like he's playing a harp only he's faster than a harp, you know, and the way -- you should -- I was looking at the way his fingers were stretched out. This guy plays some hard shit on that guitar. I mean, it is not easy what he's doing. It is not easy. It takes practice, practice, practice, practice and some more practice for what he does on
the guitar and he's been like that ever since I've been knowing him.
